evidence.snippet: 1 folds into a β6.3-helix in a lipid bilayer and forms a head-to-head dimer to function as a transmembrane channel for monovalent cations (H+, Na+, and K+)
evidence.explanation: Gramicidin A inserts into the lipid bilayer and forms transmembrane ion channels, thereby disrupting the plasma membrane barrier function.

paper.title: Gramicidin A accumulates in mitochondria, reduces ATP levels, induces mitophagy, and inhibits cancer cell growth.

evidence.snippet: upon insertion into membranes, it forms channels that disrupts ion gradients

paper.title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of stable β6.3-Helices: Discovery of non-hemolytic antibacterial peptides.

evidence.snippet: Compound 1 not only disrupted the ion concentration gradients of the plasma membrane
evidence.explanation: The gramicidin-permeabilized plasma membrane participates in aberrant ion transport; monovalent cations flow freely through gramicidin channels, dissipating normal ion concentration gradients.

paper.title: Gramicidin A accumulates in mitochondria, reduces ATP levels, induces mitophagy, and inhibits cancer cell growth.

evidence.snippet: Changes in the conductance of membranes for ions will lead to cell death

paper.title: pH dependent transfer of nano-pores into membrane of cancer cells to induce apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: Gramicidin channels inserted into the cancer cells open flux of protons into the cytoplasm and disrupt balance of other monovalent cations, which induces cell apoptosis
evidence.explanation: Gramicidin-mediated uncontrolled ion transport through the membrane causes cell death. Evidence shown in cancer cells but the ion-channel-disruption mechanism applies to bacterial cells.

paper.title: pH dependent transfer of nano-pores into membrane of cancer cells to induce apoptosis.

evidence.snippet: Povidone-iodine 1.25% ophthalmic solution was as effective as neomycin-polymyxin B-gramicidin for treating bacterial conjunctivitis
evidence.explanation: Gramicidin-containing ophthalmic solution treats bacterial conjunctivitis in a controlled clinical trial; the killing of bacteria by gramicidin underlies this therapeutic effect.

paper.title: A controlled trial of povidone-iodine to treat infectious conjunctivitis in children.

evidence.snippet: Good choices include polymyxin/gramicidin, polymyxin/trimethoprim or sulfacetamide
evidence.explanation: Clinical review identifies polymyxin/gramicidin as a recommended first-line agent for bacterial conjunctivitis in children.
